expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: TestEntryLifecycle wraps its body in synctest.Test and its three sleeps (lines 68, 85, 89) sit inside the bubble; no polling loops exist anywhere. However `Example` (line 28) calls `time.Sleep(30 * time.Millisecond)` in real time, outside any bubble — go test -v shows Example taking 0.03s wall clock while the bubbled test takes 0.00s. Example functions cannot enter a synctest bubble, but the agent chose to demonstrate expiry-by-waiting in the runnable example, so a real-time sleep with only a 10ms margin over the 20ms TTL landed in the suite. The assertion admits no carve-out: not every time.Sleep sits inside a bubble.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T

expectations.text: Documented boundaries are exercised as documented: ttl <= 0 stores without expiry, Get hides expired entries before the janitor sweeps, Close idempotence, the documented panic on non-positive janitor interval
expectations.evidence: ttl <= 0: TestEntryLifecycle stores with ttl 0 and -time.Hour and both survive elapsed time (lines 57-58, 72-77). Get-before-sweep: Example uses a one-minute janitor interval but observes the miss 30ms after a 20ms TTL, long before any sweep. Close idempotence: TestEntryLifecycle calls c.Close() explicitly (line 101) and the deferred c.Close() (line 45) runs a second time at bubble exit; a non-idempotent Close would panic and fail. Panic boundary: TestNewPanicsOnInvalidJanitorInterval covers zero and negative intervals via mustPanic.

expectations.text: The package's DOCUMENTED concurrency safety is tested as promised (this package explicitly promises concurrent use, so concurrent exercise is in-contract), without statistical race-hunting theatrics
expectations.evidence: The Cache doc promises 'All methods are safe for concurrent use.' TestConcurrentCallers has 8 goroutines each Set/Get/Len its own session key — the realistic shared-cache pattern — with no iteration-count race lotteries, no concurrent-Close hammering, no recover-hunting. go test -race -count=5 ./... passes.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
